Mountainshark (H84)

Scoring-table region: Serpentspine.

In brief: Beginning as a goblin clan founded by escaped slaves, it seeks a future in the mountains through elected leadership, mithril industry, and a war of revenge.

Narrative: high | Mission tree: medium-long (48 direct missions) | Version: local scripts support EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: very high | Early pressure: high | Expansion capacity: high.

A Clan That Won Its Freedom

Mountainshark is the playable goblin clan H84 in 1444. The English offline Wiki dates its origins to 1428, when Glozok led a group of goblins who had escaped enslavement in founding a new community. This earlier history aligns with the anti-slavery sentiment in current scripts, but its details remain attributed to the offline Wiki snapshot; later mission developments must not be presented as already completed. At the start, they are not an empire that has unified the mountains, but a small clan with a fierce will to survive and take revenge. 【Wiki】【Local history】

The Wiki gives the uprising a specific account: Glozok infiltrated a warband, secretly persuaded enslaved goblins to rise up, and used makeshift and stolen weapons, poison, and assassination to defeat their orc masters. After the revolt, he continued toward the next enslaving warband, leaving the teachings of “genius, cunning, and violence”; the clan took the name Mountainshark in his honor. They later briefly joined the Railskulker Clan, then were expelled over a dispute about the rail tithe. This is an origin story as recounted by the Wiki, not a sequence of mission steps the player must reenact. 【Wiki】

The mission tree turns this origin into an unusual national character: consolidate a foothold, gather escaped slaves, establish elected leadership based on Glozok's teachings, and invest the mountains' resources in mithril industry and the army. It is not simply a “goblin industrial state”: political legitimacy, economic technology, and revenge narratives pull on one another. Some missions and events also incorporate different groups, including trolls and kobolds, showing that the society's boundaries are not fixed at every stage. 【Local script】【Local narrative text】

The Wiki also recounts that, when later repairing the mithril hold, the goblins had no mature mining or smelting tools. They could only learn through repeated trial and error in the old foundries, even damaging parts of the hold; they then reused old dwarven cannons to speed up mining and developed a more efficient way to mint coins. This is later history on the Wiki page, resonating with the industrial theme of local missions, but it does not prove that H84 in 1444 already possesses every mithril-working technique. 【Wiki】【Local script】

Between Liberation and Revenge

The route's most important question is not a conventional war but how liberators treat former oppressors. Scripted narrative explicitly describes massacring slaveholders and erasing their cultural memory; the country therefore cannot be rated as inherently benevolent merely because it was formerly enslaved. At the same time, refuge for escaped slaves, more open political participation, and cross-cultural inclusion are genuinely present on the other side. The v2.1 assessment must retain both sets of facts: it should neither count every conquest as a crime nor excuse group-targeted harm as revenge. 【Local narrative text】

Later, the country can form Ves Udzenklan (I98; titled “The Allclan” in the formation decision) if it meets the goblin-unification requirements. This is an optional formable, and I98 has its own entry. H84-specific reforms and missions cannot be assumed to carry over unchanged after the tag switch, so this article focuses on Mountainshark itself rather than attributing every I98 story to it. 【Local decision】

How the Campaign Plays

Early on, use mobile goblin forces to seize room for survival and deal with escaped slaves and powerful neighbors. In the middle game, develop mithril, leadership institutions, and mountain industries to move the clan beyond the state of a temporary camp. Later, decide how to balance revenge, expansion, and uniting the goblin clans. Its 48 direct missions provide the feel of a substantial standalone campaign. Player discussions often describe it as combining industrial snowballing with intense narrative, but these are experiences from particular versions and do not replace current-script evidence. 【Local script】【Community opinion】

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 75/100 | Authoritarianism 36/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 28/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 74/100) | Pluralism 62/100.

The v2.1 values score is Neutral (49/100), with a mixed trajectory.

Sources, version boundaries, and the optional formable are documented on the evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Mountainshark Traditions

  • Looting speed: +50% (loot_amount; raw value 0.5).

  • Leader land shock: +1 (leader_land_shock; raw value 1).

1. Glimmers of Hope

There was once a time where goblins roamed the Serpentspine freely, without anyone to oppress them. Many clans struggled against dwarves and orcs, but none other had to endure the pain we had been subjected to. As slaves to a black orc warband we were the lowest of the low, we were worth less than the dirt we slept on. But deep in our hearts there stirred a thought. A faint memory of hope that someday we could be free once more. This hope nurtured us, strengthened our resolve. It is only through these decades of hidden resistance that we could eventually gain our freedom from the orcs.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

2. Empty Halls

The rise of Dookanson meant that almost all orc warbands had left the Serpentspine, leaving behind a gigantic power vacuum that is slowly being filled by the innumerous goblins crawling out of the eternal shadow. If we want to stay relevant in this world we must make haste and fill these empty halls with our own goblin kin who serve us and only us.

  • Settler growth: +2000% (global_colonial_growth; raw value 20).

  • National unrest: -1 (global_unrest; raw value -1).

3. Cutthroat Expertise

To survive in the harsh world of the Serpentspine the Clanboss needs only the most capable advisors around him. But in a world forged by fearsome strife and bloody battles such as the Serpentspine a simple academic is useless if they can’t fight. To prove that an advisor can survive the world they need to fight for their place. Whoever wishes to lead must defeat the one in front of him. This way only the truly strong will be the ones to advise the Clanboss on matters of state.

  • Possible advisors: +2 (advisor_pool; raw value 2).

4. Mithril Coinage

The brutal advisors of our clan demand high pay for their services which has put significant financial strain on our treasuries. To ease the burden we have supplemented their pay with coins not made of gold but of mithril, which we have in relative abundance thanks to our home, the mithril hold of Mithradhûm. This mithril coinage enables us to put our gold to other use.

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

5. Reuse Refuse

Left in the wake of the fall of Aul-Dwarov many holds and roads are full of ancient dwarven mechanisms and machinery of war. Those that have not been trashed by roaming black orc warbands can still be put to some use. Especially the old cannons and firearms are useful once they are outfitted and repaired with what we can find elsewhere. These patchwork weapons are quite hefty and to our delight we have found that they leave more than a few scars and blue spots.

  • Artillery cost: -10% (artillery_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. Innovative Mining

While drills and pickaxes are perfectly suitable tools to scratch the rock of the Serpentspine they are not much use if we want to dig down fast. For that we need to blast away all of the useless rock by firing explosives from our mithril-cannons and free the precious, shiny metals, obliterating the surrounding stone in much the same way as we did to our warband when we gained freedom. These new mining practices will show the world what it truly means to dig a mine.

  • Production efficiency: +5% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.05).

  • Development cost: -5% (development_cost; raw value -0.05).

7. The Great Shark

Our clan’s name comes from Glozok the Shark, the goblin who brought us out of slavery and into freedom. Under his leadership we have become more than a ragtag group of warriors. To this day it is his fierce wisdom that guides us and our Clanboss into the future. Each goblin of Mountainshark tries to emulate the genius, the cunning, and the incredible violence which he showed us.

  • Random candidate bonus: +1 (candidate_random_bonus; raw value 1).
